headline: Solo YouTube & podcast creators get videos down-ranked and ear-raped due to LUFS loudness discrepancies across clips and sponsors
scenario: Exporting final video edits containing multiple mixed sources: guest Zoom audio, screen recording, background music, and sponsor shoutouts
friction: Different audio clips have wildly mismatched LUFS levels (-14 LUFS vs -24 LUFS). When uploaded to YouTube and Spotify, algorithms either penalize audio clarity or blast viewer ears during sponsor transitions. Viewers complain in comments about volume jumps.

current_workaround.method: Opening Audacity or Premiere Essential Sound, manually keyframing volume sliders on 30 separate audio clips, and re-exporting 3 times.
current_workaround.drawbacks: Adds 2.5 hours of boring, non-creative manual tweaking to every video export; still occasionally gets flagged with YouTube volume reduction warnings.

cost_or_loss.summary: 10 to 12 hours wasted per month in manual waveform leveling, plus viewer retention drop-off on uneven audio transitions.

evidence_snippets: Auphonic is too clunky and upload-heavy for quick YouTube shorts. If there was a lightweight desktop drag-and-drop tool that normalized my audio stems to YouTube -14 LUFS in 5 seconds, I'd buy it on Gumroad in a heartbeat.

raw_quote: I spend more time fixing loudness spikes between my voice and sponsor reads than actually editing my video. Auphonic takes forever to upload 4GB files. Why is there no dead-simple local Mac app where I just drag an MP4 or WAV and it locks everything to -14 LUFS with zero compression artifacts? I would buy that Gumroad link immediately.
